name: Maaseiah
overview: Maaseiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known specifically as the son of Baruch. He lived in Jerusalem, situating him within the historic and spiritual center of Israel during the post-exilic period. His identity is grounded primarily in this familial and tribal context.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaseiah means 'YHWH is a refuge,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's protective nature. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, was not given directly by God but carries a significant declaration of faith in the divine character.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Maaseiah as the son of Baruch, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maaseiah's significance lies in his connection to Jerusalem and his lineage as the son of Baruch, which places him among the faithful remnant involved in the restoration of the city after the exile. His presence in the biblical record highlights the continuity of God's people in Judah and Jerusalem during a critical period of rebuilding and spiritual renewal.
